definition_en: A pattern where humans and robots delineate implicit zones in collaborative areas, adjusting positions to avoid collisions during joint assembly tasks.
A pattern where robots and humans alternate actions seamlessly in shared spaces, using pauses and cues to coordinate physical manipulations.
A pattern where humans employ multiple gestures simultaneously for robot recognition, compensating for partial misinterpretations in dynamic interactions.
A pattern where single task errors by robots diminish human confidence, leading to increased oversight in subsequent joint operations.
A pattern where robots anticipate human grasp points during object transfers, aligning paths for smooth physical exchanges without drops.
A pattern where robots exaggerate trajectories to signal intentions clearly, enabling humans to predict and coordinate shared-space movements.
A pattern where, post-mistake, robots perform bowing or retreating motions, restoring human comfort for continued task collaboration.
A pattern where humans refine gestures while robots update recognition models iteratively, enhancing accuracy in prolonged interactions.
A pattern where robots detect human hesitations in tasks and offer support, fostering smoother joint workflows in shared environments.
A pattern during physical contacts where robots modulate grip strength based on human resistance, ensuring safe collaborative handling.
A pattern where robots interpret ambiguous gestures using environmental cues, improving task coordination in cluttered workspaces.
A pattern where consistent successful handovers incrementally build human reliance on robots for routine object transfers.
A pattern where verbal clarifications following errors prompt robots to confirm understanding, realigning joint task progress.
A pattern where robots synchronize speeds with humans during approach phases, minimizing disruptions in shared physical spaces.
A pattern where humans accept minor deviations in robot pointing responses to gestures, adapting expectations over interactions.
A pattern after robot errors where humans assume lead roles temporarily, with robots yielding control for task resumption.
A pattern where robots analyze human body orientations to anticipate actions, facilitating preemptive coordination in joint tasks.
A pattern where gradual velocity reductions during transfers prevent jolts, enhancing reliability in human-robot exchanges.
A pattern where robots mirror recognized gestures back to humans, confirming interpretations and refining mutual communication.
A pattern where repeated collaborations develop aligned task representations, reducing coordination overhead in complex joint efforts.
A pattern where dynamic safety margins expand around robots in crowded spaces, allowing humans to navigate freely alongside.
A pattern where humans blame external factors over robot flaws post-failure, preserving trust for future interactions.
A pattern where combining speech with gestures boosts robot comprehension, streamlining commands in noisy shared environments.
A pattern where success in simple handovers bolsters confidence for more complex joint manipulations involving robots.
A pattern where extended pauses by robots indicate processing, giving humans time to interject during collaborative sequences.
A pattern where robots signal inaccessible areas via gestures, prompting humans to reposition for effective joint access.
A pattern where humans initiate recovery by repeating commands clearly, guiding robots back into synchronized task flow.
A pattern where robots align limb swings with human rhythms, creating fluid tandem movements in assembly lines.
A pattern where humans introduce novel gestures incrementally, with robots learning them through contextual task repetitions.
A pattern where robots propose weight distributions via visual cues, optimizing human-robot partnerships in lifting tasks.
A pattern where sudden human slowdowns cue robots to halt, preventing overreach in shared-space navigations.
A pattern where robot verbal apologies after errors increase human willingness to continue joint activities promptly.
A pattern where robots track human gazes to attended objects, enhancing gesture-based object selection accuracy.
A pattern where small successes post-failure gradually rebuild handover reliability perceptions in repeated trials.
A pattern where familiarity with robots raises thresholds for acceptable proximity during intense coordination phases.
A pattern where humans perform exaggerated motions for robots to imitate, bootstrapping new task capabilities collaboratively.
A pattern where robots cap applied forces during interactions, allowing humans to override physically if needed.
A pattern where humans verbally override incorrect gesture interpretations, training robots in real-time feedback loops.
A pattern where shared visual indicators confirm mutual task objectives, streamlining physical coordination efforts.
A pattern where proactive robot actions after human cues reduce latency, enhancing efficiency in joint workflows.
A pattern where relaxed human stances signal robot takeover, while alert postures prompt assistance offers.
A pattern where robots rotate objects to preferred human grasp angles, facilitating seamless physical transitions.
A pattern where reviewing past mistakes with humans strengthens robot explanations, aiding trust restoration.
A pattern where task demands trigger fluid shifts between human lead and robot support in evolving collaborations.
A pattern where robots monitor peripheral human motions, preparing responses without direct addressing.
A pattern where high trust levels stabilize handover speeds, but require maintenance to avoid complacency.
A pattern where specific robot motions post-error convey reset states, encouraging human re-engagement.
A pattern where synchronized acceleration curves between partners minimize jitter in shared transport tasks.
A pattern where robots weigh gesture likelihoods by task phase, resolving conflicts in multi-command scenarios.
A pattern where real-time trajectory swaps ensure collision-free paths for humans and robots in tight spaces.
